Short answers up front:
- We can reserve +8 GPUs in your existing pool with start date 2026-11-01 provided we agree on the ramp schedule and commit window.
- We can offer a committed baseline of 6,000 tokens/sec measured at the pool level, with a documented burst allowance.

What we'd like to confirm before producing draft addendum text:
1) Measurement point: do you want token/sec measured at pool egress (Redwood edge) or at customer-visible API (post-ingress) — we typically recommend edge measurement for consistency.
2) Percentile for SLO: our standard is 95th percentile over a calendar month, but we can discuss 99th or an MTTD-based approach.
3) Remediation: our usual model is service credits tied to % of monthly committed fee, scaled to duration and severity.

Karthik — can you draft the SLO language and a short fallback playbook (model variant fallback + brief auto-scale behavior) for Claire to review? Marissa — once we have agreed language we'll push a single addendum PDF and Docusign link.

Hi Claire, Sean — looping in the ops details here. Draft notes below; I can turn these into contract-ready language once we confirm the measurement point and percentile.

Draft SLO summary (technical):
- Metric: Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) measured at Redwood egress per Reserved Pool (aggregate across reserved GPU instances).
- Guarantee: 6,000 tokens/sec sustained, where sustained is defined as the 95th percentile of 60-second sliding-window averages across the calendar month.
- Burst allowance: up to 30% above committed baseline (max 7,800 tokens/sec) for individual 60-second windows, not to exceed 10 such windows per 24-hour period.
- Measurement details: tokens are counted according to our standard tokenizer byte-level tokenization (UTF-8 BPE); both prompt and generated tokens count. Measurements exclude retries and duplicated requests from client-side retries (we dedupe by request-id header).
- Fallback and mitigation: if the pool falls below the committed baseline for more than 3 consecutive 5-minute windows (measured at 60s granularity), Redwood will: 1) auto-route new requests to a compatible lower-cost model variant for up to 30 minutes to preserve client throughput; 2) trigger scale-up of reserved burst capacity (subject to pool headroom and GPU availability).
- Remediation (service credit): if committed baseline is not met for >60 cumulative minutes in a calendar month (after applying the burst allowance), customer is eligible for service credits equal to 5% of monthly committed Reserved Pool fee per additional hour of unremediated degradation, capped at 50% of monthly fee.

Operational notes / lead times:
- Procurement & provisioning: GPU reservation changes require a 14-day lead time for topology changes in Dedicated regions; we recommend confirming by 2026-10-17 for a Nov 1 start.
- Testing window: we can schedule a 2-day acceptance test in week 1 of November to validate throughput under your traffic curves.

Attachments: I have prepared a first-pass addendum PDF (heliometrics_reserved_pool_addendum_draft_v1.pdf) with the above text plus an appendix with measurement examples. I've also included a short ops checklist for the November ramp.

If this matches your expectations I will convert to legal-friendly wording and Marissa will start the doc/DocuSign flow.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference

2) Percentile: 95th makes sense for now.

Can you add an explicit escalation timeline: Redwood acknowledges within 30 minutes of threshold breach and provides an ETA for remediation within 2 hours, after which credits apply if unresolved.

- Insert the operational acknowledgement & ETA language above.
- Provide the DocuSign-ready PDF by 2026-10-12 so our contracts team can route it before renewal.
